context: Inventory every fake, stub, and monkeypatched boundary in tests/ and tests/fake_hrana.py. For each, ask what would still pass if the implementation were subtly wrong, and record the answer. Prefer strictness: doubles should reject unexpected arguments, unexpected call counts, and unexpected orderings rather than tolerate them. Where a double stands in for a real external tool, either assert the real tool's documented interface or add a clearly marked opt-in check that exercises the real one. Fix the doubles whose looseness hides a plausible defect and record the rest as accepted with reasoning. Do not rewrite the suite; this is a targeted audit with a written result.
description: Two independent defects in the same helper let twelve provider tests pass against a resolver that could not drive a real secret store. _provider_script wrote the two-character sequence backslash-n instead of a line break, collapsing every stub to a single malformed shell line, and every stub was written to accept whatever arguments it was handed, so appending a positional argument that breaks security, op, and pass went unnoticed until an external review. The suite was green throughout. Other doubles in this repository carry the same risk: FakeLibsql and FakeHrana stand in for a backend whose real behaviour they define rather than observe, and any stub written to satisfy the code under test proves only that the code calls what the author expected. Audit them and pin the ones that matter.

anti_patterns.dont: Encode a line break as an escaped sequence inside a generated script or fixture
anti_patterns.instead: assemble multi-line fixtures from real newlines and assert the fixture behaves as intended
anti_patterns.why: the fixture collapses to one malformed line and the test then exercises a shell parse error rather than the logic it names

anti_patterns.dont: Treat a green suite as evidence that a double is faithful
anti_patterns.instead: ask what would still pass if the implementation were wrong, and record the answer
anti_patterns.why: a double written to match the implementation will always agree with it

anti_patterns.dont: Write a stub that accepts any arguments so the test passes
anti_patterns.instead: make the double reject anything it was not told to expect
anti_patterns.why: a permissive double tests that the code calls something, not that it calls the right thing, which is exactly how the appended-capability defect survived twelve tests

preserves.behavior: Any check that needs a real external tool is opt-in and skips loudly when the tool is absent.
Existing coverage is not deleted to make an audit finding go away.
Test runtime stays within the existing fast-suite expectation; strictness must not turn into network or tool dependence in the default suite.
